Learned Addl. P.P., Mr. R. Saha is present on behalf of the State-respondent.

This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. corresponding to Section 528 of BNSS is filed for setting aside the order dated 21.11.2025 passed by Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.5,
West Tripura, Agartala in connection with Criminal (Misc) 176 of 2025.

Taking part in the hearing, Learned Counsel for the petitioner, Mr. Agniva Chakrabarti drawn the attention of the Court that initially this accused was arrested by police and was produced before the Court of Learned CJM, West Tripura, Agartala, on 26.07.2025 and on that day, Learned CJM cancelling the bail application remanded the accused till 28.07.2025 and on 28.07.2025 on perusal of the case diary, Learned CJM, West Tripura, Agartala granted interim bail to the accused till 15.09.2025 and challenging the order of Learned CJM, the defacto complainant, i.e. the victim moved an application to the Court of Learned Additional Sessions Judge, West Tripura, Agartala as mentioned above seeking cancellation of the interim bail granted to the accused and thereafter, after hearing by order dated 21.11.2025 Learned Addl.

sentences.text: It is further submitted by Learned Counsel for the petitioner-accused that along with this application another application for staying operation of the order passed by Learned Additional Sessions Judge, West Tripura, Agartala dated 21.11.2025 is filed and at this stage, if the order impugned is not stayed then the petitioner would be seriously prejudiced.

entities.text: Learned Additional Sessions Judge, West Tripura, Agartala
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: So, Learned Counsel for the petitioner prayed before this Court to stay the operation of the said order exercising the inherent power provided under Section 528 of BNSS.

On the other hand, Learned Addl. P.P. appearing on behalf of the State submitted that there is very little scope to entertain the application under Section 528 of BNSS against the order dated 21.11.2025 passed by Learned Addl. Sessions Judge, West Tripura, Agartala, Court No.5.

entities.text: Addl. Sessions Judge, West Tripura, Agartala
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He further submitted that after the order dated 21.11.2025 the accused is presently without any bail and no separate bail application was moved on behalf of the said accused.
So, in such a situation, there is no scope to entertain the application filed by the petitioner-accused.

At the time of hearing, Learned Counsel for the petitioner referred few citations of different High Courts and drawn the attention of the Court the scope for entertaining such an application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. corresponding to Section 528 of BNSS.
I have perused the citations.

Hon'ble the Supreme Court of India in a recent case in Abhimanue Etc. Etc. vs. State of Kerala reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 2037, in para Nos.14 and 15, observed as under:
"14.

entities.text: Abhimanue Etc. Etc. vs. State of Kerala reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 2037
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before proceeding further, we consider it appropriate to begin our analysis by addressing one of the arguments raised by Mr. Chakraborty.
He has challenged the very maintainability of the application filed before the High Court.

According to him,
once an application under Section 439(2), Cr.P.C. seeking cancellation of bail has been rejected by the Sessions Judge, a second application under the same provision cannot be filed directly before the High Court.

Instead, the proper course would be either to challenge the Sessions Judge's order in a petition for revision, or to invoke the inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482, Cr.P.C.
15.
We are unable to agree with this argument.
We note that, in the present case, the application before the High Court was filed under "Section 482 r/w 439(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure".
That being the case, nothing prevented the High Court from exercising its inherent powers."

From the aforesaid observation, it appears that Hon'ble the Apex Court in such a situation observed that High Court has got the scope to exercise inherent power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
In this regard, Hon'ble High Court of Kolkata in a case reported in (1999) SCC OnLine Cal 44 (Mahesh Mahato & Ors. vs. Sri Sankar Kumar Mahato & Anr.) in C.R.R. 2748 of 1998 observed that the power under Section 482 can be exercised in the special circumstances.

entities.text: (1999) SCC OnLine Cal 44 (Mahesh Mahato & Ors. vs. Sri Sankar Kumar Mahato & Anr.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similarly, Hon'ble High Court of Alahabad in a case reported in (2015) SCC OnLine All 7137 (Surendra Kuwar Singh vs. State Sri Sandip Khanna vs The State Of Tripura & Ors on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190964948/
2 of U.P. and Others) also observed in the same manner.

entities.text: (2015) SCC OnLine All 7137 (Surendra Kuwar Singh vs. State Sri Sandip Khanna vs The State Of Tripura & Ors on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
So, after hearing both the sides and also after going through the aforesaid observation made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and also by the different High Courts, it appears to this Court that challenging the order of the Learned Additional Sessions Judge, the present petitioner-accused has got the scope to invoke the jurisdiction of the High Court provided under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
corresponding to Section 528 of BNSS.
Accordingly, the present application filed on behalf of the accused is admitted for hearing.
Let notice be issued upon the respondents.
Since, Learned Addl. P.P. has appeared on behalf of respondent Nos.1 & 2, so, issuance of formal notice in respect of respondent Nos.1 & 2 is waived.
The petitioner-accused may take steps for service of notice upon the respondent No.3 both by normal process and also by registered A/D post within three(3) days and file proof of service.
Call for the record of West Agartala, Women P.S. case No.38 of 2025 pending before the Court of Learned CJM, West Tripura Agartala.

entities.text: Court of Learned CJM, West Tripura Agartala
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: List the matter on 12.12.2025.
Till next date, the operation of the impugned order dated 21.11.2025 passed by Learned Additional Sessions Judge, West Tripura, Agartala, Court No.5 be stayed.
